documents.text:
**SHOCKER IN COLLEGE HOOPS: Canadian Hockey Legend Bob Gracie Makes Surprise Switch to NCAA Basketball**

In a stunning turn of events, Canadian ice hockey icon Bob Gracie has traded in his skates for sneakers, announcing his decision to join the NCAA Division I men's basketball league. The news sent shockwaves through the sports world, leaving fans and pundits alike scratching their heads. Gracie, a four-time Stanley Cup champion and Hockey Hall of Famer, revealed his unexpected career shift in an exclusive interview with our publication. "I've always had a passion for basketball, and I figured, why not give it a shot?" the 62-year-old Gracie said with a chuckle. "I'm not getting any younger, but I'm still competitive as ever. I want to see if I can bring some of that hockey magic to the hardwood." Gracie, who last played professionally in the NHL in 1983, has been quietly working on his basketball skills in recent months. According to sources close to the situation, he's been training with a private coach and has made significant strides in his game. "I've been impressed with Bob's work ethic and dedication," said University of Michigan head coach Juwan Howard, who reportedly offered Gracie a walk-on spot on the Wolverines' roster. "He's got a natural athleticism that translates well to the court. We're excited to see what he can bring to our team." Gracie's decision has sparked a heated debate among sports enthusiasts, with some hailing the move as a bold experiment and others dismissing it as a publicity stunt. However, the numbers suggest that Gracie may be more than just a novelty act. According to data from his training sessions, Gracie has posted impressive stats, including a 40-inch vertical leap and a 3-point shooting percentage of 42%. "I think people are underestimating Bob's potential," said ESPN analyst Jay Bilas. "He's got the size, strength, and competitive drive to make an impact in the NCAA. It's not like he's trying out for the NBA – this is college basketball, and I think he can hold his own." Gracie is set to make his NCAA debut on November 15, when the University of Michigan takes on arch-rival Ohio State.
